newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to widen irrigation curbs on drought fears.
newsitem.headline: France to widen irrigation curbs on drought fears.

text.p: Authorities in the Cher and Indre regions in central France plan this week to start limiting the amount of water farmers can use to irrigate their crops, local government officials said on Thursday.
The action will bring the number of provinces or departments hit by such restrictions to 13.
A three-month dry spell has forced farmers to tap the water table for crop relief.
Irrigation curbs will take effect on Saturday in the Cher and possibly as soon as Thursday in the Indre region.
Farmers and gardeners, who grow fruit, flowers, vegetables and tobacco or operate fish farms are being exempted in the Cher.
Soybean growers and fish farm operators are also being exempted in the Indre region.
The new rules mean farmers are prevented from tapping rivers to irrigate their crops two days a week in the Cher and one day a week in the Indre.
Areas now covered by partial irrigation bans include Cote d'Or, Essonne, Eure-et-Loir, Loir-et-Cher, Loiret, Oise, Yvelines, Seine et Marne, Somme, Pas-de-Calais and Charente.
The curbs could be extended to Orne, Limousin and Poitou-Charentes after the Environment Ministry holds a meeting of its drought committee on April 29.
